A1.justification: Shared authors, subject matter, and retained passages establish the same research work despite retitling and substantial revision. Both PDFs are readable and complete for comparison, including v2's Appendix A; v4 has no appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 report the authors' LLMSanitize evaluations of Guided Prompting and Sharded Likelihood across six benchmarks, explicitly stating that they ran the library on 100 test data points.

after.justification: The LLMSanitize experiments are removed. Results throughout v4 are attributed to cited studies; its tables summarize published contamination findings and classify methods, without reporting original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new detection algorithm. V4 expands its review of existing algorithms, while retained detectors keep their described procedures. Removing the LLMSanitize implementation contribution changes technical documentation and contribution scope, without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: V4 removes the authors' entire evaluation coverage: ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, Winogrande, and GSM8K in v2 Table 1. These datasets may remain discussed, but are no longer evaluated by this work. Newly surveyed benchmarks are literature coverage, not additional author-run experiments.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison between Guided Prompting and Sharded Likelihood in v2 Table 1 disappears. Both methods remain reviewed in v4, but their participation in the authors' empirical comparison is removed; newly cited detectors are not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V4 removes v2's 100-test-point evaluation protocol using four 7B models—Llama-2, Qwen-1.5, Mistral, and Gemma—and GPT-3.5-turbo for Guided Prompting only. The associated ROUGE-L and likelihood-based testing setup has no replacement author-run evaluation.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, sensitivity studies, or robustness experiments. V2's removed table is a regular benchmark evaluation. V4's added discussion of membership-inference failures summarizes cited studies rather than introducing supplementary experiments by this work.

E5.justification: V2 Table 1 reports p-values for two statistical detection methods and marks statistically nonsignificant results. V4 removes this entire original statistical-reporting component. Its retained descriptions of statistical tests concern cited methods, not uncertainty reporting for its own experiments.

E6.justification: All 54 p-value entries in v2 Table 1 are removed, including HellaSwag Sharded Likelihood values printed as 0.000 for all four 7B models. V4 adds attributed literature findings, but provides no corresponding rerun or replacement results for the removed experiments.

T1.justification: V4 Section 3.4.1 adds the mathematical definition of Min-K%++ from Zhang et al., including expected log-probability and standard-deviation normalization in Equation 2. Equation 1 mainly formalizes the existing Min-K% Prob description. Neither version contains theorem proofs.

C1.justification: V2 claims both a comprehensive survey and the release of LLMSanitize as a central contribution. V4 removes the library contribution from the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion, and instead emphasizes a finer taxonomy and coverage through early 2025 of over 50 techniques and 100 relevant papers.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive limitations concerning membership inference: temporal distribution shifts can masquerade as membership signals, and performance can collapse under better-controlled distributions. It also discusses Min-K% Prob's parameter and token-frequency limitations, distinguishes gray-box access, and identifies contamination benchmarks lagging contemporary evaluation needs.

D1.justification: V4 removes the library access information and all of Appendix A, including installation instructions, Python 3.9/CUDA 11.8 recommendations, llmsanitize version 0.0.8, checker arguments, and the two-GPU vLLM setup. This establishes loss of implementation and access guidance from the paper, not that the software itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands research coverage with RECALL, CAMIA, EM-MIA, Min-K%++, and critical membership-inference studies, among others. It explicitly distinguishes its detection-focused survey from concurrent surveys by Palavalli, Deng, and Fu. Library-related references are removed alongside that contribution.

P1.justification: The document is retitled and substantially reorganized into finer subsections. Existing Guided Prompting/DCQ material moves into model memorization, while DICE moves into model confidence. The library section and usage appendix disappear, and the introduction and conclusion are reframed, although many survey paragraphs remain.

P2.justification: V4 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, substantially expands Figure 1's taxonomy, and introduces literature-summary and model-access tables. V2's empirical Table 1 and appendix code listings are removed; the later Table 1 serves a different purpose.

improvement.justification: V4 improves critical survey coverage through its membership-inference discussion, temporal-shift cautions, and finer method classification. However, it withdraws v2's central LLMSanitize contribution, implementation guidance, and direct detector evaluations. These changes trade stronger critical synthesis for reduced practical utility and empirical illustration. The PDFs support both effects, but do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
